states.name: Alabama
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized; general prohibitions on selling game apply.
states.howTo: No permit or salvage tag program found. Contacting a local ADCNR Conservation Enforcement Officer before keeping an animal is the prudent course.
states.timing: No reporting deadline found. Possession of freshly killed protected game appears lawful only during that species' open season.
states.excluded: Protected nongame, state or federally listed species, and MBTA birds. Out-of-season protected game (per 220-2-.24).
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific roadkill provision for turkey or upland birds; same open-season possession rule (220-2-.24) would apply. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act.
states.otherRestrictions: Alabama has CWD carcass import and transport restrictions; check current ADCNR CWD rules.
states.citation: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.24 (general possession rule; not roadkill-specific)
states.agency: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries

states.name: Alaska
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited. Meat is for personal use only; it may not be sold or used as animal feed or bait.
states.howTo: The driver must notify Alaska State Troopers or Alaska Wildlife Troopers (DPS) as soon as possible. Salvage teams (2 or more people, each 18+, living in the area) apply through the DPS/AWT online roadkill program. When called, a team must accept immediately and arrive within about 30 minutes.
states.timing: Notify troopers as soon as possible after the collision. In Anchorage and Mat-Su, salvagers must submit a 5-inch lower jaw section and the antlers to ADF&G within 14 days. DPS may require annual reapplication.
states.excluded: No species list published. The program addresses moose; other big game is handled at trooper discretion.
states.gameBirdsNote: No roadkill-specific provision found for grouse or ptarmigan. Migratory birds (waterfowl, cranes and others) are federally protected under the MBTA and cannot be possessed without a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: The entire animal and all remains must be removed from the scene; incomplete removal can lead to a citation and removal from the program. Edible meat must be salvaged for human consumption.
states.citation: 5 AAC 92.220(b) (big game killed or injured by a vehicle is state property; driver must notify); 5 AAC 92.210 (game as animal food or bait)
states.agency: Alaska Department of Public Safety, Alaska Wildlife Troopers (with ADF&G)

states.name: Arizona
states.saleOfParts: The permit holder may gift the carcass or parts. Sale is not authorized by 17-319, and Arizona's general prohibitions on selling wildlife apply.
states.howTo: A peace officer or authorized AZGFD employee issues a big game salvage permit to the driver or to another person who wants the carcass. The officer completes the form, gives the original to the recipient and sends a copy to AZGFD within 48 hours. The permit is free and non-transferable.
states.timing: Must have the permit before possessing or transporting the carcass. The issuing officer forwards a copy to AZGFD within 48 hours. No seasonal limit.
states.excluded: Non-big-game species are not covered. No permit may be issued if the animal is suspected to be diseased or spoiled.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is big game in Arizona, so the big game salvage permit covers it. The statute does not cover small game or upland birds (quail, grouse, pheasant). Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: The permit does not certify the meat as edible, and the issuing officer, agency and AZGFD are not liable. Possessing a carcass under a fraudulently obtained permit is a class 1 misdemeanor.
states.agency: Arizona Game and Fish Department

states.name: Arkansas
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized; general AGFC prohibitions on selling game apply.
states.howTo: Call the AGFC Radio Room at 800-482-9262 to report the animal and receive an official salvage tag number.
states.timing: The salvage tag number must be obtained before possessing the animal or any part, starting at the point of initial contact. No seasonal limit stated.
states.excluded: The rule names only deer, adult gobblers and bear. Possession of other species is not addressed. Elk are big game in Arkansas but are not named in the vehicle-accident subsection. Endangered species are protected (Code 05.27).
states.gameBirdsNote: Adult gobblers (wild turkey) are expressly covered by the same report-and-salvage-tag rule. No roadkill provision found for other upland birds. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: AGFC CWD Management Zone carcass-movement restrictions apply. Secondary sources say antlers may not be removed unless the deer has been tagged and checked.
states.citation: AGFC Code 05.18(E), Big Game Checking Requirements (Ark. Code R. 002.01.22-032)
states.agency: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission

states.name: California
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited.
states.howTo: None available. The planned web-based salvage permit was never implemented.
states.timing: Not applicable.
states.excluded: All species. Even the never-implemented pilot was limited to deer, elk, pronghorn and wild pig, and excluded protected species.
states.gameBirdsNote: No salvage allowed. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit. The pilot would not have covered birds.
states.otherRestrictions: Under Fish & Game Code § 2000.5, only authorized state or local agencies may remove animals accidentally killed on roadways.
states.citation: Cal. Fish & Game Code §§ 2000.5, 2000.6 (SB 395, Stats. 2019, ch. 869)
states.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife / Fish and Game Commission

states.name: Colorado
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized by the rule; general prohibitions on selling wildlife apply. CPW may charge the donee actual processing costs for processed meat.
states.howTo: Notify CPW (nearest field office) or another authorized agency to obtain a free donation certificate. CPW may require the animal to be presented for inspection. Beneficial-use letters of authorization are issued by the Director.
states.timing: Notify CPW within 48 hours of taking possession. Secondary reporting says the office visit to obtain the certificate follows within a reasonable time.
states.excluded: MBTA species; federal or state threatened or endangered species; species whose possession is otherwise prohibited by statute or regulation. Raptors and eagles are excluded through the MBTA and the federal eagle act.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey and upland birds are not expressly excluded, so they appear possessable with a CPW donation certificate. Species covered by the federal MBTA (waterfowl, doves, cranes) are excluded by the rule.
states.otherRestrictions: CPW advises not approaching or dispatching an injured animal. Colorado CWD carcass handling rules apply.
states.citation: 2 CCR 406-0, Chapter W-0, Article X, #016(C)-(E)
states.agency: Colorado Parks and Wildlife

states.name: Connecticut
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed by § 26-86; general prohibitions on selling game apply.
states.howTo: Call local police, state police or DEEP EnCon Police. The officer inspects the animal and issues a Wildlife Kill Incident Report, and the possessor keeps a copy.
states.timing: Inspection and report are required before taking possession. No seasonal limit.
states.excluded: All species other than deer, moose and black bear.
states.gameBirdsNote: The statute covers only deer, moose and black bear. No provision found for turkey or upland birds, so possession is not authorized. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: The vehicle operator has first right to the animal.
states.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 26-86; see also § 26-82(a) (no violation when a deer is struck by a motor vehicle)
states.agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP), Wildlife Division / EnCon Police

states.name: Delaware
states.saleOfParts: Delaware generally prohibits selling deer or deer parts (only hides of lawfully killed and checked deer may be sold).
states.howTo: Call DNREC Division of Fish & Wildlife Natural Resources Police (302-739-4580) or State Police. An officer examines the deer and issues a vehicle-killed deer tag.
states.timing: The tag is required before possession. No specific hour deadline found.
states.excluded: All species other than deer.
states.gameBirdsNote: No roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds, so possession is not authorized. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: The deer must be examined and tagged by an officer.
states.citation: 7 Del. C. § 794 (as cited by the Nevada LCB memo; not independently verified)
states.agency: Delaware DNREC Division of Fish & Wildlife (Natural Resources Police); Delaware State Police

states.name: Florida
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized; general FWC prohibitions on selling wildlife apply.
states.howTo: None required for deer under the rule.
states.timing: No deadline or seasonal limit for deer.
states.excluded: All species other than deer, including black bear, Florida panther, Key deer (federally endangered), turkey, furbearers and protected species.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not covered. Wild turkey and other game bird roadkill may not be possessed. Migratory birds are covered by the MBTA and need a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: Report vehicle-killed bears and panthers to FWC; possession is not allowed.
states.citation: Fla. Admin. Code R. 68A-4.004(4)
states.agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC)

states.name: Georgia
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized by § 27-3-28; Georgia's general restrictions on selling wildlife apply.
states.howTo: No permit for most species. For bears, report to the Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division or any law enforcement officer, who forwards the report to DNR within 48 hours.
states.timing: Bear reports are due within 48 hours of taking possession. No seasonal restriction.
states.excluded: Species protected under O.C.G.A. Title 27, Ch. 3, Art. 5 (state protected species) or federal law, including endangered species and MBTA birds such as raptors.
states.gameBirdsNote: Native game birds such as turkey and quail fall under the general native-wildlife allowance. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the MBTA, and the statute excludes federally protected species.
states.otherRestrictions: Georgia DNR CWD carcass import rules apply to deer from outside the state.
states.agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division

states.name: Hawaii
states.saleOfParts: Not allowed (no lawful possession).
states.howTo: None. No salvage permit exists. Contact DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife or DOCARE for dead or injured wildlife.
states.timing: N/A
states.excluded: All wildlife by default. Endangered native species (e.g., nene, Hawaiian hoary bat) are strictly protected.
states.gameBirdsNote: No salvage provision found for game birds (pheasants, francolins, quail, wild turkey, etc.). Migratory birds (including the federally/state-listed nene) are protected under the federal MBTA and cannot be possessed without a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: Hawaii restricts possession and inter-island transport of axis deer to stop their spread (2012 law and later legislation). Roadkill on state highways is removed by HDOT.
states.citation: No specific roadkill statute found. General wildlife possession rules are in HRS ch. 183D and HAR 13-123 (hunting).
states.agency: Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources (DLNR), Division of Forestry and Wildlife (DOFAW)

states.name: Idaho
states.saleOfParts: Parts other than edible flesh of big game, upland game animals, upland game birds and furbearers may be bought or sold. Bighorn sheep parts may not be bought, bartered or sold.
states.howTo: Self-report online through the IDFG roadkill salvage form, which generates a printable CE-51 Wildlife Salvage Permit at no cost. You can also call an IDFG regional office or conservation officer. After hours, leave your name, phone, address and salvage location and a permit will be mailed. The permit must accompany the salvaged wildlife.
states.timing: Notify IDFG within 24 hours of salvage and obtain the salvage permit within 72 hours. Year-round, with no season restriction.
states.excluded: Protected nongame wildlife, threatened or endangered species (e.g., grizzly bear, Canada lynx), federally protected migratory birds, and any species not lawfully hunted or trapped.
states.gameBirdsNote: Upland game birds (pheasant, grouse, quail, partridge, wild turkey) may be salvaged with the same report and permit. Migratory birds, including waterfowl and doves, are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Since July 1, 2018, a person may dispatch wildlife severely injured in a collision. Safety and traffic laws must be followed. CWD Management Zones have special salvage and carcass transport rules. Salvaged meat is consumed at your own risk.
states.citation: Idaho wildlife collision salvage rule (IDFG rule effective 2012; dispatch authority added 2018). The Nevada LCB 2025 memo cites Idaho Code § 36-506. Exact IDAPA section not verified.
states.agency: Idaho Department of Fish and Game (IDFG)

states.name: Illinois
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited for vehicle-killed deer: no part may be bartered or sold. Furbearer pelts taken in season by a licensed person follow normal fur rules (not separately verified).
states.howTo: Deer: submit the IDNR 'Claim a Road Kill Deer' online report and receive a Report ID. Keep the Report ID until all parts are consumed or disposed of, and show it to a peace officer on request. No salvage tag is required. Taxidermists, tanners and processors must record the Report ID and label the deer with it. Furbearers: hold the appropriate hunting or trapping license, habitat stamp and permits.
states.timing: Report deer possession within 24 hours. Furbearers may be taken only during that species' open season.
states.excluded: Non-residents may not claim deer. Wildlife other than deer and in-season furbearers is not covered. Threatened or endangered species, raptors and migratory birds are excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific roadkill salvage provision found for wild turkey, pheasant or other upland birds. Assume possession is not authorized without Conservation Police Officer (CPO) permission. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Killing a deer crippled by a vehicle is illegal without CPO permission. Deer found dead or injured by other means may not be transported until a CPO grants permission. A head, antlers or hide kept while green or in commercial processing must carry an irremovable tag from a CPO.
states.citation: 17 Ill. Adm. Code 750.10 (Deer Killed by a Motor Vehicle); 520 ILCS 5/2.30 (furbearers, added by HB 3178 in 2011).
states.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR)

states.name: Indiana
states.saleOfParts: Not verified. Title stays with the state under IC 14-22-10-5, so assume sale is not allowed.
states.howTo: Call or flag down a law enforcement officer or DNR conservation officer, who issues a possession permit (sometimes called a road-kill permit). Keep the permit with the meat until it is consumed. DNR Law Enforcement dispatch can help.
states.timing: Obtain the permit before removing or possessing the animal. No specific report deadline was found in official sources.
states.excluded: Endangered or threatened species (state and federal), migratory birds and raptors. Bobcat and other protected species are likely excluded (unverified).
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is reportedly covered by the same possession-permit approach (secondary sources only). No separate upland bird provision was found. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Do not approach or kill an injured animal. Call 911 or police, and an officer may dispatch it. Intentionally hitting an animal is illegal taking. CWD carcass import rules apply to cervids from other states.
states.citation: IC 14-22-10-5 (title to accidentally killed wild animals stays in the state). The administrative rule section authorizing officer-issued possession permits was not located.
states.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Division of Fish & Wildlife and Division of Law Enforcement

states.name: Iowa
states.saleOfParts: Generally prohibited. Salvage is for human consumption or animal feed. Hides, feathers and antlers are treated only as a 'secondary benefit', and peace officers may not salvage game solely for financial gain. Sale or trade of the carcass is not allowed except as permitted by law.
states.howTo: Immediately contact the nearest DNR conservation officer, Iowa State Patrol trooper, sheriff's department or police department and request a salvage tag before taking possession. The tag must be signed by the holder and a peace officer or designee and must stay with the animal until consumed. Tags are non-transferable and valid only for the period stated.
states.timing: Contact an officer immediately and get the tag BEFORE taking possession.
states.excluded: Spotted fawn deer and hen pheasants. Protected nongame, endangered and threatened species, and migratory birds are not salvageable.
states.gameBirdsNote: Game birds such as pheasant and wild turkey are covered as 'game', except hen pheasants, which are expressly not salvageable. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: The entire carcass must be removed from the scene. CWD carcass import rules apply to cervids brought into Iowa.
states.citation: Iowa Code § 481A.11; 571 Iowa Admin. Code ch. 80 (80.1 Salvage; 80.2 Game killed by motor vehicles).
states.agency: Iowa Department of Natural Resources (DNR)

states.name: Kansas
states.saleOfParts: Not explicitly addressed. Assume no sale of salvage-tagged big game or turkey parts, consistent with general prohibitions on selling game meat.
states.howTo: Request a department salvage tag from a KDWP game warden. Kansas Highway Patrol troopers and sheriff's deputies can also issue them. The tag records the recipient's name and address, tag number, species, sex, location, date, time and cause of death, and is signed by the issuing agent. Meat may be donated under the salvage tag number.
states.timing: Get the tag before or at the time of possession. No specific hour deadline was found.
states.excluded: Threatened or endangered species (e.g., lesser prairie-chicken where listed), raptors, migratory birds and nongame protected species. Furbearers out of season.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is covered by salvage tags like big game. Other upland birds (pheasant, quail, prairie chicken) may be possessed only in season with a license and within limits. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: The salvage tag must stay with the carcass. KDWP CWD rules apply to carcass transport and importation.
states.citation: K.A.R. 115-4-2(a)(4) (big game and wild turkey; salvage tags).
states.agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks (KDWP)

states.name: Kentucky
states.saleOfParts: Not verified. Kentucky generally prohibits selling wildlife meat. Assume no sale.
states.howTo: Reportedly, notify KDFWR (1-800-858-1549) or a conservation officer, giving the species and location. No named permit was found.
states.timing: Reportedly within 24 hours for deer and within 48 hours for black bear. Unverified.
states.excluded: Federally and state listed endangered species, migratory birds and raptors. Bear may have special reporting requirements.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is reportedly treated like deer: report it. No separate upland bird provision was found. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Remove the entire carcass and do not intentionally hit wildlife. CWD rules under 301 KAR 2:095 restrict importing and transporting cervid carcasses and parts.
states.citation: Not located. Likely in KRS ch. 150 or 301 KAR ch. 2 (possibly 301 KAR 2:095 or 2:172); unverified.
states.agency: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (KDFWR)

states.name: Louisiana
states.saleOfParts: Not allowed.
states.howTo: Call LDWF Enforcement (statewide hotline 1-800-442-2511, or the regional office) or a game warden at the scene and get permission before taking the animal. No formal named permit was found.
states.timing: Permission must come before possession.
states.excluded: All wildlife unless an agent authorizes possession. Endangered species (e.g., Louisiana black bear, which is delisted but protected), raptors and migratory birds.
states.gameBirdsNote: No salvage provision found. Possession of wild turkey or other game birds outside lawful hunting is illegal without agent authorization. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Illegal possession can carry fines of roughly $400 to $950 and up to 120 days in jail, per media reports (not quoted from LDWF). LDWF CWD carcass import and transport rules apply.
states.citation: No specific roadkill statute found. General illegal possession of wildlife under La. R.S. Title 56; exact section unverified.
states.agency: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF), Enforcement Division

states.name: Maine
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed in the statute. Assume sale is not allowed.
states.howTo: Report to any law enforcement officer (game warden, state police, sheriff or local police), who investigates and issues a certificate or possession permit. A warden is not required.
states.timing: Report immediately ('by the quickest means'). The certificate must be issued before the carcass is removed.
states.excluded: Canada lynx, owls and other birds of prey, all threatened or endangered species, and federally regulated migratory birds.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is covered by the same report-and-certificate requirement. No salvage authorization was found for other game birds (e.g., ruffed grouse). Waterfowl and other migratory birds go to the USFWS (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Taking only part of a deer, moose or bear carcass is a civil violation ($100 to $500), as is failing to report. Repeat violations can be a Class E crime. Possessing any wildlife without a permit is illegal. Collision tags count toward deer mortality data used to set antlerless permit numbers.
states.citation: 12 M.R.S. § 12403 (Damage to motor vehicles by wild animals or wild birds).
states.agency: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife (MDIFW) and Maine Warden Service

states.name: Maryland
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed in the regulation. Assume no sale of deer or turkey meat. Separately, DNR issues commercial 'Deer Salvage Permits' to businesses that remove dead deer.
states.howTo: Attach a homemade field tag, then report through the DNR internet-based checking system or another method listed on the DNR website (phone check). Keep the confirmation number and give it to DNR on request. Once you have a confirmation number, the field tag is no longer needed while the animal stays in your possession.
states.timing: Report within 24 hours of taking possession. Deer must be reported before the head or hide is removed, and turkey before it is processed for consumption.
states.excluded: Species other than deer and wild turkey are not covered (e.g., black bear, furbearers out of season). Endangered or threatened species, raptors and migratory birds.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is covered by the same rule: field tag, then register within 24 hours and before processing for consumption. No provision was found for other upland birds. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: Keep a record of the confirmation number. CWD carcass transport restrictions apply in Maryland's CWD Management Area and to imported cervid carcasses.
states.citation: COMAR 08.03.04.03(D) (Forest Wildlife: deer or turkey killed by means other than hunting); authority Md. Code, Nat. Res. §§ 10-205, 10-415.
states.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Wildlife and Heritage Service

states.name: Massachusetts
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited. No sale, barter or exchange for payment. The person may keep the head, hide, hooves and shinbones for personal use.
states.howTo: On taking possession, immediately notify the Office of Law Enforcement (Environmental Police) of the intent to salvage, giving name, address, and the date, time and place of the kill. If that office cannot be reached, notify local police or the nearest State Police barracks and ask that the incident be logged. Then bring the carcass to a MassWildlife or OLE office, or to an Environmental Police Officer at a location the officer names. The officer attaches a seal and issues a free salvage permit.
states.timing: Notify immediately on taking possession. The carcass must be presented for sealing and the permit within 24 hours of the kill. The seal stays on until the deer is butchered, and the permit is kept until all edible parts are consumed.
states.excluded: All species other than deer, which the regulation does not cover. Non-residents and people who were not in the striking vehicle may not take a deer themselves.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not covered. 321 CMR 2.04 applies only to deer, and no salvage provision for wild turkey or upland birds was found, so possessing them would need separate authorization. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves, woodcock) are federally protected under the MBTA and cannot be possessed without a federal permit.
states.otherRestrictions: Massachusetts domicile is required. If the eligible person declines the deer, an Environmental Police Officer may give it to an approved nonprofit or to another Massachusetts-domiciled person, under a permit in the recipient's name. Inedible deer must be buried or incinerated.
states.citation: 321 CMR 2.04 (Salvage, Disposition and Possession of Deer Killed by Means Other than by Sport Hunting)
states.agency: Massachusetts Division of Fisheries and Wildlife (MassWildlife) / Office of Law Enforcement (Massachusetts Environmental Police)

states.name: Michigan
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed in the salvage statute. Michigan law generally bars selling game, so assume sale is prohibited, though this was not confirmed.
states.howTo: Free DNR online salvage permit (Survey123 form linked from the DNR roadkill page), giving the date, location and intended use. The permit is emailed. Alternatively, a salvage tag from the DNR or the investigating officer. Questions go to the DNR Wildlife Division Permit Specialist at 517-284-6210.
states.timing: The statute requires 'prompt' notification or a tag and sets no fixed hourly deadline that was found. No seasonal limit was found.
states.excluded: Badger, bobcat, brant, coot, crow, cub bear, duck, elk, fisher, Florida gallinule, geese, marten, moose, otter, snipe, sora rail, spotted fawn deer, Virginia rail, wild turkey, wolf, woodcock, and endangered or threatened species (which fall under Part 365).
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is expressly excluded. So are ducks, geese, brant, coot, snipe, woodcock, sora and Virginia rail, Florida gallinule and crow. 'Small game' (which appears to include pheasant, grouse and quail) may be salvaged with a written record, per the statute's small-game category. Migratory birds are also barred federally under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: The driver has first priority. Salvage does not apply to anyone who intentionally kills or injures game with a vehicle. The DNR Director may suspend salvage in disease areas (CWD or bovine TB). Taking antlers from a roadkill deer without a permit is illegal possession.
states.citation: MCL 324.40115 (added by 2014 PA 255, SB 613). The DNR also cites MCL 324.43539 and Wildlife Conservation Order section 4.5, which were not verified.
states.agency: Michigan Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Wildlife Division

states.name: Minnesota
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed on the DNR page. General Minnesota game laws restrict sale of wild animal meat, so assume sale is prohibited, though this was not confirmed.
states.howTo: Free possession permit from a DNR conservation officer, the State Patrol, a county sheriff or another law enforcement officer, usually at the scene. Permits are valid for 6 months. DNR enforcement lines: 888-646-6367 or 651-296-6157.
states.timing: The permit is valid for 6 months. No reporting deadline in hours was found, but the permit must be obtained before possessing or transporting the animal.
states.excluded: Not codified. Protected, threatened or endangered species presumably cannot be possessed, but this was not confirmed.
states.gameBirdsNote: No bird-specific statute was found. Permits are reportedly issued for 'many other animals', so turkey or upland birds would be at the issuing officer's discretion (unconfirmed). Migratory birds cannot be possessed without a federal MBTA permit.
states.otherRestrictions: The road authority removes deer that are not salvaged. In CWD management zones, carcass movement restrictions apply: only certain parts may leave the zone, and whole carcasses must stay for testing. Possessing roadkill without a permit can bring misdemeanor charges.
states.citation: Minn. Stat. 97A.502 (Deer killed by motor vehicles)
states.agency: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Enforcement Division

states.name: Mississippi
states.saleOfParts: Sale of wild game meat is generally prohibited in Mississippi (assumed). Not confirmed for roadkill.
states.howTo: No formal salvage permit was found. The recommended practice is to contact an MDWFP conservation officer or local law enforcement.
states.timing: None found.
states.excluded: Endangered or protected species (federal and state). Out-of-season game possession may be an issue.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific rule was found. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA. Wild turkey should not be possessed out of season without MDWFP authorization (assumed).
states.otherRestrictions: Deer carcasses may not be dumped on roadsides; this is littering, with a fine of up to $250. Mississippi bans importing whole cervid carcasses from out of state because of CWD (40 Miss. Code R. 2-2.7). In-state CWD management zone carcass rules may apply.
states.citation: None specific found. The CWD carcass import rule is 40 Miss. Code R. 2-2.7.
states.agency: Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks (MDWFP)

states.name: Missouri
states.saleOfParts: Not confirmed for roadkill. Shed antlers not attached to the skull may be bought and sold without authorization. Sale of wildlife meat is generally prohibited.
states.howTo: Contact the local MDC conservation agent, who issues a free written authorization (Wildlife Dispensation Permit).
states.timing: Report to an agent within 24 hours to receive possession authorization; MDC states this explicitly for antlered deer heads and road-killed deer.
states.excluded: Not specified. Endangered species and protected wildlife are presumably not authorized.
states.gameBirdsNote: No road-killed turkey rule was found. Possessing any wildlife found dead generally needs agent authorization under the Wildlife Code. Migratory birds are barred federally under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: CWD carcass movement and testing rules may apply in CWD management zones. Wildlife taken illegally cannot be possessed (3 CSR 10-4.141).
states.citation: Wildlife Code of Missouri, 3 CSR 10. The exact roadkill or found-dead section was not confirmed; Chapter 10 (antlers) is referenced by MDC.
states.agency: Missouri Department of Conservation (MDC)

states.name: Montana
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited. The meat must be used for human consumption (not bait) and may not be sold. The Montana Food Bank Network does not accept roadkill.
states.howTo: Free Vehicle-Killed Wildlife Salvage Permit, from on-scene law enforcement or online through FWP. The permit must be printed (an electronic copy on a phone is not accepted), signed and carried.
states.timing: Get the permit within 24 hours of taking possession. No seasonal limit.
states.excluded: All species other than deer, elk, moose and antelope, including bear, bighorn sheep, mountain goat, bison, furbearers and birds.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not allowed. Salvage is limited to the five big game species, so upland birds, turkey and waterfowl may not be salvaged (migratory birds are also barred federally under the MBTA).
states.otherRestrictions: The entire carcass, including entrails, must be removed from the roadway; field dressing is allowed only if all parts are taken away. The salvager may not kill an injured animal, but an officer may, after which it can be salvaged. Unusable parts must go to a legal disposal site, and dumping within 200 yards of a road or public property is illegal. Hunting carcass tags may not be used on roadkill. CWD carcass transport rules may also apply (not stated on the FWP page).
states.citation: MCA 87-3-145; MCA 75-10-212 (disposal); MCA 87-6-302 to 304 (false statements)
states.agency: Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks (FWP)

states.name: Nebraska
states.saleOfParts: Selling or trading meat is prohibited. The hide, hair, hooves, bones, horns and antlers of roadkill deer, antelope or elk may be sold. Processed meat may be given away with a receipt showing the permit information.
states.howTo: Notify Nebraska Game and Parks. A Conservation Officer or designee tags the carcass with a two-part salvage tag: Part 1 goes to the district office, and Part 2 stays with the carcass or meat.
states.timing: Notify within 24 hours of picking up the carcass. The officer tags it within 48 hours of notification. The permit is valid for up to 90 days.
states.excluded: All big game other than deer, antelope and elk (e.g., bighorn sheep, mountain lion), plus protected and endangered species. Any carcass showing evidence of being shot.
states.gameBirdsNote: No roadkill salvage provision for birds. Found-dead parts of upland game birds may be possessed but not sold, and feathers may not bear shot marks. Wild turkey is not specifically addressed. Migratory birds are barred federally under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Nebraska residents only. Individuals may hold only one roadkill carcass at a time. No processing for preservation before the permit is obtained.
states.citation: 163 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 4, section 013
states.agency: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission

states.name: Nevada
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed in SB 215. The failed 2021 bill (AB 299) would have banned sale. Unconfirmed under the current regulation.
states.howTo: Free NDOW wildlife salvage permit under Commission regulation. The application method (online or officer) is not confirmed.
states.timing: The draft CGR 5.27 revision (August 2026) changes the reporting or permit deadline from 48 hours to '2 business days'. The final adopted text is unconfirmed.
states.excluded: Draft: black bear and crow. The Commission may halt salvage permits if CWD is detected in Nevada. Protected and endangered species are presumably excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: The bill text sets no species limit. The draft CGR 5.27 excludes crows. Upland bird and turkey eligibility under the final regulation is unconfirmed. Migratory birds are barred federally under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Salvage permits may be suspended if CWD is detected in Nevada. Other conditions (whole-carcass removal, restricted highways) are unconfirmed for the final regulation.
states.citation: SB 215 (2025), Statutes of Nevada 2025, ch. 184 (new section in NRS ch. 501; amends NRS 502.150 and 503.030); Commission General Regulation 5.27 (wildlife salvage permit), under revision
states.agency: Nevada Department of Wildlife (NDOW) / Board of Wildlife Commissioners

states.name: New Hampshire
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed. Assume sale is prohibited (unconfirmed).
states.howTo: Complete the department form, available from a conservation officer or any NH law enforcement officer, and submit it to a conservation officer for approval. If no officer is available, call Fish and Game dispatch at 603-271-3361 for instructions. Keep the approved copy with the meat. Moose and other protected wildlife may also need a Special Wildlife Permit (Fis 1102.01).
states.timing: The permit is valid for 6 months and can be extended once for another 6 months. No specific hours-based deadline was found.
states.excluded: Not enumerated in the rule. Threatened or endangered species presumably cannot be possessed.
states.gameBirdsNote: The rule covers 'wildlife' generally. Wild turkey is reportedly salvageable under the same permit (secondary source). Migratory birds cannot be possessed without a federal MBTA permit.
states.otherRestrictions: New Hampshire residents only. The applicant acknowledges receiving the animal and releases the department from liability for whether it is safe to eat.
states.citation: N.H. Admin. Rules Fis 1102.02 (also Fis 1102.01 for moose and protected wildlife). The underlying RSA was not confirmed.
states.agency: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department

states.name: New Jersey
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed. The permit allows keeping the deer for consumption or transferring it to another person for that purpose. Sale is presumed prohibited (unconfirmed).
states.howTo: Report the collision to police promptly. State or municipal police issue a possession permit on a Division of Fish and Wildlife form. Butchers may also require registration with the state by phone or online, with a confirmation number, before processing.
states.timing: Report promptly to police. The permit is valid for 90 days from issue.
states.excluded: All species other than deer, including bear.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not covered. New Jersey's roadkill provision applies only to deer, so turkey, pheasant and other birds may not be salvaged under it. Migratory birds are barred federally under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: The collision must be reported to police. Permits come from the police department of the municipality where the deer was found.
states.citation: N.J.A.C. 7:25-17.6 (Possession of dead deer)
states.agency: New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife (NJDEP); permits issued by State or municipal police

states.name: New Mexico
states.saleOfParts: The public may not sell. NMDGF itself sells salvaged animals to members of the public.
states.howTo: Call the local conservation officer or NMDGF dispatch. The officer decides whether the animal can be salvaged and issues a receipt (fee goes to the Game Protection Fund). There is no online roadkill permit.
states.timing: No statutory deadline found. Practical limit: before the meat spoils.
states.excluded: Not specified. Protected or endangered species would not be released. Only animals the officer judges fit for consumption are salvaged.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds. Treat as requiring conservation-officer permission. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves, etc.) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Unauthorized possession of protected game is a violation. CWD carcass-transport rules may apply to deer and elk.
states.citation: No specific roadkill statute or NMAC rule identified. General possession prohibitions in NMSA Chapter 17 apply.
states.agency: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish (NMDGF)

states.name: New York
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized by 11-0915. The general prohibition on selling wild game applies.
states.howTo: Report the collision to an Environmental Conservation Officer, State Police, the county sheriff or local police. The officer investigates and issues a possession permit, which may also allow transfer to a person the owner designates.
states.timing: Report within 24 hours of the collision.
states.excluded: Species other than deer, moose and bear are not covered by this provision. Endangered or threatened species are excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: ECL 11-0915 covers only deer, moose and bear. No roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds, so possession of other dead wildlife generally needs DEC authorization. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Applies to unintentional collisions that damage a vehicle. NY CWD rules restrict importing carcasses from outside the state.
states.citation: NY Environmental Conservation Law § 11-0915
states.agency: NYS Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)

states.name: North Carolina
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited, except that licensed trappers and hunters may sell certain furbearers (e.g., beaver, coyote, raccoon) found during the open season to licensed fur dealers. Fox sales have extra conditions.
states.howTo: Deer: ask the officer who investigates the collision for authorization. Deer or turkey found dead: contact NCWRC (Customer Service 833-950-0575 or a wildlife officer). Bear: NCWRC possession permit. Elk: written NCWRC authorization. The former Possession and Salvage permit is no longer needed for most other wildlife.
states.timing: No specific deadline found. Authorization should be obtained before possession or transport.
states.excluded: Endangered, threatened and special concern species require a permit. Raptors and migratory birds require federal permits. Bear and elk require specific Commission permission.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey killed accidentally or found dead: possession requires authorization from a Commission employee (the NCWRC page also lets the investigating officer authorize road-killed turkey). Other non-listed wildlife found dead may be possessed without a permit under 10B .0127(f). Raptors and migratory birds need a federal USFWS permit.
states.otherRestrictions: Deer authorization covers personal use, including giving the carcass to another person for private use or to a charity. NC CWD carcass-transport rules apply.
states.agency: North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission (NCWRC)

states.name: North Dakota
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed. General ND law restricts sale of big game parts. Not confirmed.
states.howTo: Free possession permit from a game warden or a local law enforcement office.
states.timing: Permit must be obtained before taking possession. No other deadline found.
states.excluded: Not specified in NDGF guidance. Endangered and threatened species and migratory birds are excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific roadkill provision found. Possessing protected birds outside season likely requires warden authorization. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Carcass waste may not be left on public property (roads, ditches, WMAs). Landfill disposal is recommended. ND CWD carcass-transport rules apply.
states.citation: No specific NDCC section confirmed. Based on NDGF news releases.
states.agency: North Dakota Game and Fish Department

states.name: Ohio
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized by the statute. Ohio general law prohibits selling deer meat. Not confirmed for hides and antlers.
states.howTo: Report the collision to a wildlife officer or other law enforcement officer, who issues a certificate of legal ownership (the possession receipt).
states.timing: Report within 24 hours of the accident.
states.excluded: The statute covers only deer. Possession of other species is not authorized by it. Endangered species are excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: ORC 1533.121 covers only deer. A 2013 House Bill reportedly proposed extending it to wild turkey and wild hogs, but its passage was not confirmed. Treat turkey and upland birds as requiring officer authorization. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: The right belongs to the driver who struck the deer. Others get the deer only through an officer's certificate. Ohio CWD rules on carcass import and transport may apply.
states.citation: Ohio Revised Code § 1533.121
states.agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife

states.name: Oklahoma
states.saleOfParts: Not allowed per third-party sources (meat may be given away). No official confirmation found.
states.howTo: Contact the county game warden (ODWC), who may issue a permit or receipt to possess the carcass.
states.timing: Contact the warden before moving or possessing the animal. Third-party sources mention 24 hours, but no official source confirms it.
states.excluded: Endangered and threatened species. Others are at warden discretion.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific provision found. Warden permission is presumed necessary for turkey and other game birds. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Take the entire animal and dispose of the carcass properly.
states.citation: No specific statute or OAC rule identified. General possession rules are in 29 O.S. (Oklahoma Wildlife Conservation Code).
states.agency: Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation (ODWC)

states.name: Oregon
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited. Parts may be transferred with a written Wildlife Transfer Record.
states.howTo: Free online Roadkill Salvage Permit through the MyODFW electronic licensing system (guest or ODFW ID). Apply after taking possession.
states.timing: Apply within 24 hours of taking possession. Surrender the head and antlers to an ODFW office within 5 business days (call ahead).
states.excluded: Cougar, black bear, pronghorn, bighorn sheep, Rocky Mountain goat, and white-tailed deer outside the allowed areas. Columbian white-tailed deer are excluded outside those areas. Licensed furtakers may salvage certain furbearers during open seasons under separate rules.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not covered by the salvage program. Game birds may not be salvaged. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Intentionally hitting an animal is illegal. Remove the entire carcass, including the gut pile, from the road and right-of-way. Antlers may not be kept. Only an enforcement officer, or the striking driver, may dispatch an injured animal (ORS 498.016). Heads are tested for CWD. ODFW does not inspect the meat.
states.citation: OAR 635-043-0175 (Roadkill Salvage Permit); ORS 498.016 (SB 372, 2017)
states.agency: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife (ODFW)

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.saleOfParts: Not allowed. Consumption permits prohibit transfer, and inedible parts must be surrendered or disposed of as the Commission directs. Salvaged furbearer parts may be used under a furtaker license (sale generally follows furtaker rules).
states.howTo: Call PGC at 1-833-PGC-HUNT or 1-833-PGC-WILD for the deer or turkey permit number. Other wildlife: discretionary consumption permit from PGC (valid up to 120 days). Furbearers: holders of a valid furtaker license may keep road-killed furbearers.
states.timing: Within 24 hours of taking possession. A consumption permit is valid up to 120 days.
states.excluded: Bear and elk are not covered by the self-claim provision. River otter, bobcat and fisher are excluded from furbearer salvage. Threatened and endangered species are excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is treated the same as deer: possess immediately, then call PGC within 24 hours for a permit number (residents only). Other game birds need a discretionary consumption permit. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Residents only. Edible parts may not leave the residence except for processing. Furbearers killed in the closed season must be reported within 24 hours. In CWD Disease Management or Established Areas, remove the head and backbone before transporting the deer outside the area.
states.citation: 58 Pa. Code § 147.142 (with 34 Pa.C.S. authority)
states.agency: Pennsylvania Game Commission (PGC)

states.name: Rhode Island
states.saleOfParts: Meat may not be sold or donated to licensed retail or manufacturing facilities. Meat must be used for consumption, not bait.
states.howTo: File a WRS report online at dem.ri.gov/wildlife-salvage-permit or by phone at 401-789-0281. Provide species, estimated age and sex, a photo, location, and date/time. One permit per animal.
states.timing: Within 24 hours of collecting the animal. Keep the permit until the meat is packaged and frozen or the hide is skinned and stretched.
states.excluded: Any species not on the list. Allowed list: white-tailed deer, wild turkey, pheasant, coyote, red fox, gray fox, rabbit, beaver, squirrel, muskrat, raccoon, fisher, woodchuck, mute swan. Fisher and fox have additional requirements.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey, pheasant and mute swan are on the salvage list. Other birds are excluded, and migratory birds need a federal permit (the mute swan is non-native and not MBTA-protected).
states.otherRestrictions: Do not kill injured animals. Only law enforcement may dispatch them. Do not use hunting tags on salvaged animals. Remove the entire animal from the roadway (field dressing allowed, but leave no parts). Dispose of unused parts properly. Holders consent to inspection.
states.citation: 250-RICR-60-00-14 (effective 03/25/2025). Enabling legislation S2810 (2024).
states.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM), Division of Fish and Wildlife

states.name: South Carolina
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed. SC generally prohibits selling game meat.
states.howTo: Contact the SCDNR Law Enforcement communications center (803-955-4000) for authorization. Report road carcasses for removal to SCDOT (855-GO-SCDOT).
states.timing: No official deadline found.
states.excluded: Black bear (report to SCDNR) and endangered or threatened species. Others are unclear.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific provision found. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA. Turkey possession outside season likely needs SCDNR authorization (unverified).
states.otherRestrictions: Unclear. SCDOT handles carcass removal on state roads.
states.citation: None identified
states.agency: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR)

states.name: South Dakota
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited. No part may be sold, bartered or traded.
states.howTo: Contact a local GFP conservation officer, who may issue a dated written authorization (no fee). The authorization must stay with the carcass during processing and storage.
states.timing: Must contact the officer before taking possession. A person who euthanizes a seriously injured animal must report it to GFP within 24 hours.
states.excluded: Anything other than deer and antelope is not covered (elk, bighorn sheep, mountain goat, bison, game birds, furbearers, protected and endangered species).
states.gameBirdsNote: No roadkill provision for game birds (pheasant, turkey, grouse, etc.); the statute covers only deer and antelope, so possessing road-killed game birds is not authorized by it. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves, cranes) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: SD law separately allows a person to humanely euthanize a seriously injured animal, with a report to GFP within 24 hours. CWD rules: if deer or elk carcass parts leave the county of origin, remains must go to a waste-management provider or permitted landfill. No dumping in road ditches or on public land.
states.citation: SDCL 41-1-5.7 (deer and antelope killed by motor vehicle)
states.agency: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks (GFP)

states.name: Tennessee
states.saleOfParts: Personal use only. The statute says 'for personal use', so sale is not authorized.
states.howTo: Deer and turkey: notify TWRA or local law enforcement (a phone call is sufficient), giving name and address. Bear: a TWRA officer must authorize and issue a kill tag before possession.
states.timing: Within 48 hours for deer (and turkey per TWRA guidance). Bear: before possession. No seasonal limits.
states.excluded: Federally protected wildlife and species protected under T.C.A. Title 70 Chapter 8 (state endangered, threatened and nongame protected species), including raptors and migratory birds. Bear only with an officer-issued tag.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey: TWRA guidance (via a 2022 news report) says to notify TWRA or law enforcement within 48 hours, the same as deer. The statute's general allowance ('a wild animal killed by motor vehicle') seems to cover other resident game birds. Migratory birds and other federally protected birds are excluded by the statute and by the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Motorists are not required to report game they hit. Violations are a Class C misdemeanor. Normal CWD carcass-transport rules apply, including restrictions on moving carcasses out of CWD Management Units.
states.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 70-4-115(c)
states.agency: Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (TWRA)

states.name: Texas
states.saleOfParts: Prohibited
states.howTo: None. No salvage permit exists. Report injured deer to a TPWD game warden dispatcher.
states.timing: N/A
states.excluded: All wildlife. Since a 2007 change, even nongame road-surface collection is not allowed.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not allowed (same prohibition). Migratory birds are also federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: A person may move a deer they are sure is dead off the road but may not keep it. Injured animals: contact a game warden.
states.citation: General Texas Parks & Wildlife Code possession prohibitions (illegal means and methods). A 2007 change tied to HB 12 (80th Legislature) removed the prior nongame roadkill allowance. No single roadkill-specific section was confirmed.
states.agency: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD)

states.name: Utah
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized. Sale of big game parts is restricted under R657-5-20.
states.howTo: Contact DWR (regional office or conservation officer) before removing the animal. Possession may be authorized at officer discretion, for example by donation slip or certificate of registration. Report roadkill locations with the Utah Roadkill Reporter app (reporting only, not a salvage permit).
states.timing: Before possession. No statutory deadline found.
states.excluded: Unclear. Antlers or horns attached to a skull plate may not be possessed without DWR authorization; use the Deadhead Reporter. Endangered and threatened species and raptors are not salvageable.
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific roadkill provision found. Protected game birds (turkey, upland) would need DWR authorization. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: CWD carcass importation and transport rules apply (R657-5-43, R657-5-18).
states.citation: No roadkill-specific rule confirmed. General possession rules: Utah Code Title 23A (Wildlife Resources Act) and Utah Admin. Code R657-5 (big game) and R657-3 (possession of protected wildlife).
states.agency: Utah Division of Wildlife Resources (DWR)

states.name: Vermont
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized. Sale of big game meat is generally prohibited.
states.howTo: Call 911 or state police dispatch, which contacts the game warden. The warden issues a tag (a unique 5-digit number) before the animal is removed.
states.timing: Must obtain warden authorization before removal.
states.excluded: Not formally listed. Endangered and threatened species and protected birds are excluded. Furbearers and other species need warden authorization (secondary sources say a possession tag is needed for big game and furbearers).
states.gameBirdsNote: No specific roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds. Possession of game without a license or authorization is generally prohibited, so contact a warden. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Only wardens or listed officials may kill a deer injured beyond recovery (10 V.S.A. § 4749), with disposal under § 4513. Wardens collect teeth from bear and moose for biological data. Transporting roadkill across state lines is reportedly illegal. Vermonters only, per a 2015 news report.
states.citation: 10 V.S.A. § 4749 (injured deer killing, disposal under § 4513). No roadkill-specific possession statute confirmed.
states.agency: Vermont Fish and Wildlife Department

states.name: Virginia
states.saleOfParts: For the claimant's own use. Sale is not authorized (general game-sale prohibitions apply).
states.howTo: Report to a conservation police officer (DWR) or local law enforcement. The officer inspects the animal and issues a call-for-service or report number.
states.timing: Must report immediately. Allowed year-round.
states.excluded: Only deer, bear, turkey and elk are covered. All other species (furbearers, small game, nongame, protected and endangered species, raptors) are not authorized under this section.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is covered on the same terms as deer, bear and elk. Other game birds are not covered. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: An animal injured badly enough to need euthanasia may be awarded after officer inspection. Virginia's CWD carcass-transport restrictions still apply, including moving carcasses out of Disease Management Areas.
states.citation: Va. Code § 29.1-539 (Claiming deer, bear, turkey, or elk struck by motor vehicle)
states.agency: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources (DWR)

states.name: Washington
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed on the WDFW page. Sale of salvaged game is presumed not allowed under general wildlife-sale prohibitions (unverified).
states.howTo: Free printable Roadkill Salvage Permit through WDFW's online application, or at WDFW regional offices. Keep the signed, dated hardcopy with the meat until all edible parts are consumed. Big game hunting licenses and tags cannot be used.
states.timing: Permit within 24 hours of taking possession. Eastern Region (100-series GMUs): submit CWD samples (head with at least 3 inches of neck, or lymph nodes) within 5 days of receiving the permit.
states.excluded: All species except deer and elk. Columbian white-tailed deer are always excluded.
states.gameBirdsNote: Not covered. Only deer and elk may be salvaged. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: The entire carcass, including entrails, must be removed from the right-of-way. Only law enforcement or WDFW-authorized people may euthanize injured animals; the public may not kill an injured animal to salvage it. No trespassing. CWD transport limits apply (WAC 220-413-030), and carcasses may not cross WA/OR/ID/BC lines unless criteria are met. Unfit meat and parts go to disposal under WAC 246-203-121.
states.citation: WAC 220-400-040 (Possession of dead wildlife; salvage provisions now in subsection (4)); RCW 77.15.750 (penalties); WAC 220-413-030 (CWD and carcass transport)
states.agency: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW)

states.name: West Virginia
states.saleOfParts: Not specified in the statute. Sale of wildlife is generally prohibited in WV, so presume no sale.
states.howTo: Notify an appropriate law-enforcement agency, then obtain a free non-hunting game tag from WVDNR (Electronic Licensing / Check Game system or a DNR office). The tag must be attached to the carcass.
states.timing: Notify law enforcement within 12 hours of the incident. Obtain the non-hunting game tag within 24 hours of taking possession.
states.excluded: Elk, spotted fawns, bear cubs and protected birds (plus state and federal endangered species).
states.gameBirdsNote: Game birds such as wild turkey and grouse appear to be covered by the general 'wildlife' language. 'Protected birds' are excluded, and migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: The collision must be accidental or inadvertent. Statewide CWD carcass-transport rules apply (restrictions on moving carcasses out of CWD Containment Areas).
states.citation: W. Va. Code § 20-2-4(e)
states.agency: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources (WVDNR)

states.name: Wisconsin
states.saleOfParts: Not authorized. General prohibitions on sale of wild game apply.
states.howTo: Deer and turkey: vehicle-killed registration online through DNR GoWild (gowild.wi.gov/wildlife/harvest/carkill) or by phone at 608-267-7691. Bear: call the DNR law-enforcement non-emergency line for a tag. Tags are free.
states.timing: Deer and turkey: register before removal from the scene. Bear: tag within 24 hours of receiving officer instructions. Small game: open season only.
states.excluded: Fisher, otter, bobcat, wolf, migratory birds, and protected, endangered and threatened species. Elk is not covered.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey: same as deer. Register with DNR before possessing or removing it from the scene; the driver has priority. Other small game, including upland birds: only during the open season and only if the person holds the required hunting or trapping license. Migratory birds are excluded and federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Deer must comply with CWD carcass-transport rules (NR 10). Small-game possession requires the appropriate license and an open season. Carcass removal from roadways is requested through the local Sheriff.
states.citation: Wis. Stat. § 29.349 (Animals killed by motor vehicles); § 29.354 (possession exemption)
states.agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR)

states.name: Wyoming
states.saleOfParts: Not addressed in Chapter 70. Wyoming generally prohibits sale of game meat, so presume no sale (unverified).
states.howTo: Electronic authorization through the WGFD Roadkill Collection Application or the 'Report Roadkill' button in the Wyoming 511 app (requires a WGFD username). A certificate issues immediately after a short questionnaire and works without cell service. The rule also allows a permit, donation coupon or Interstate Game Tag.
states.timing: Authorization before taking possession. Collection only from sunrise to sunset.
states.excluded: All species except antelope, deer, elk, moose, wild bison and wild turkey (for example bighorn sheep, mountain goat, bears, mountain lion, wolves, furbearers and other game birds). Excluded locations: Interstates 25, 80 and 90, active construction and maintenance zones, and National Park Service roads.
states.gameBirdsNote: Wild turkey is covered with authorization. Other upland birds (grouse, pheasant, partridge) are not covered. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
states.otherRestrictions: Remove the entire animal (edible and inedible parts) from the right-of-way. No field dressing in the right-of-way. Park at least 2 feet off the roadway with flashers on. Present the animal for inspection on request. No entering private property without permission. The rule does not authorize euthanizing injured animals. CWD (deer, elk, moose): whole carcasses may not leave Wyoming; the head and spinal column must go to an approved landfill or incinerator unless taken to a CWD sampling site; only listed parts (boned meat, cleaned hide, cleaned skull or antlers, teeth, finished mounts) may be transported. False statements are a violation.
states.citation: Wyoming Game and Fish Commission Regulation Chapter 70, Possession of Road Killed Wildlife (authority W.S. 23-3-106, 23-3-310)
states.agency: Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD)
